subject: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — HealthScope
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthscope.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@healthscope.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — HealthScope

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Goal: Evaluate model fit for HealthScope's triage assistant (clinical intake + sensitive guidance avoidance). Primary constraints are accuracy on domain-specific phrasing, low hallucination on patient instructions, and robust refusal behavior for out-of-scope clinical advice.
- Current assets you mentioned: 12k annotated triage examples, a small in-house prompt library, and a SOC 2 requirement for vendor evidence.
- Success metrics: F1 > 0.78 on triage intent classification, refusal rate >= 95% on attempted medical-diagnosis prompts (per safety spec), and P99 latency < 400ms for single-turn inference.

Suggested immediate next steps (per our discussion):
1) I'll share an initial recommended model shortlist and the benchmark link so your team can run an early pass.
2) We’ll provide a first-pass prompt set tuned for safety/refusal behaviors (attached as healthscope_prompt_set_v1.txt).
3) Schedule a short SE workshop (30–45m) to run live evals and review the initial results.
4) We’ll prepare a redacted SOC 2 excerpt and security questionnaire answers for your compliance team.

Attached: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt set + expected refusal labels).
Benchmarks: https://drive.redwood.com/healthscope/evals/model-benchmarks-20260304 (read-only).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Dev (SE) to coordinate the workshop and share the baseline benchmark run we did. Are you available Tue/Wed next week for the workshop?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.txt (6 KB) - prompt examples + refusal test cases

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@healthscope.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 18:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — HealthScope

Thanks Marissa — super helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The annotated triage examples are in CSV (12,317 rows) with intent labels and an anonymized notes column — happy to share a redacted sample.
- Compliance will expect the SOC 2 artifact and also a short description of data retention and log access policies.
- For the safety/refusal checks: we currently have a small set (~200) of ‘edge-case’ prompts that historically trigger risky completions. Can Redwood run the refusal tests against the recommended models and share confusion matrices?

We’re available Tue 10 Mar 10:00–11:00am PT or Wed 11 Mar 2:00–3:00pm PT for the workshop. Please include an SE who can run the evals live and walk us through common failure modes.

Also — curious about your recommended model shortlist and whether you think a smaller quantized model will meet our latency targets without compromising refusal/safety behavior.

Best,
Aisha
Director of Product, Clinical Systems
HealthScope

Attachment: Request to share redacted CSV sample (will follow separately)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthscope.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@healthscope.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — HealthScope

Hi Aisha —

Perfect — locking in Tue 10 Mar 10:00am PT for the workshop (calendar invite sent). Dev will run the live evals. Below is the initial recommendation and links to the baseline benchmark we ran on a synthetic slice mirroring your triage data: 

Recommended model shortlist (first-pass):
- redwood-llama-70b-v2 (fp16) — best on intent accuracy, strong contextual understanding; higher cost.
- redwood-llama-13b-q4 (int8/quant) — promising throughput and latency; we saw modest degradation on nuanced clinical phrasing in our synthetic tests.
- open-med-small-3b — lightweight baseline for latency-sensitive endpoints; expect lower coverage on rare intents.

Benchmarks (baseline run): https://drive.redwood.com/healthscope/evals/model-benchmarks-20260304
Summary highlights from our baseline CSV (attached as healthscope_model_benchmarks.csv):
- 70b-v2: intent F1 0.82, hallucination on medication instructions 1.2%, refusal success 96.8%
- 13b-q4: intent F1 0.75, hallucination on medication instructions 3.9%, refusal success 92.1%
- open-med-small-3b: intent F1 0.68, hallucination 5.4%, refusal 88.3%

Safety/refusal evaluation notes: 
- We ran the standard refusal harness (see docs: https://docs.redwood.com/evals/refusal-harness) and a set of guardrail prompt injections (sensitive_domain_injection tests). Results indicate the 70b-v2 meets your 95% refusal target on our synthetic set; the quantized 13b variant is close but fails more often on targeted adversarial prompts.
- Next step in the workshop: run your 200 edge-case prompts and your redacted sample to produce a confusion matrix and per-prompt trace logs. Those traces will help us create tuned guardrail prompt templates (included in the prompt set) and to recommend a fallback routing policy for ambiguous cases.

Attachments: healthscope_model_benchmarks.csv, soc2_cert_redacted.pdf

I’ve included Laura (CS) to surface any existing incident/retention policies and Rishi for commercial questions (if you want pricing/committed capacity options post-eval).

See you on Tue.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachment: healthscope_model_benchmarks.csv (12 KB)
Attachment: soc2_cert_redacted.pdf (110 KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dr. Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — HealthScope

Hi all —

Quick tech note ahead of Tuesday’s workshop:

- For the live evals I’ll provision a dedicated endpoint running redwood-llama-70b-v2 (fp16) and a side-by-side 13b-q4 quantized instance so we can compare traces in real time.
- Please upload the redacted CSV sample to the Drive link before EOD Mon (so we can pre-run the confusion matrices). I’ll also run your 200 edge-case prompts through the refusal harness and attach per-prompt trace outputs to the Drive folder.
- Regarding quantization impact on safety: our internal experiments show quantization sometimes impacts token-level logit calibration, which can change refusal thresholds. We’ll produce per-prompt probabilities and tuned guardrail templates to compensate; where necessary we recommend fallback routing to the larger model for high-risk prompts.

Deliverables for the workshop:
- Per-model confusion matrices and ROC-style plots (baseline vs your sample)
- Per-prompt trace logs and suggested guardrail prompt patches
- Suggested routing policy (cost/latency tradeoffs) and an initial pricing estimate for a dedicated pool if you want consistent P99 latency.

If there are any special compliance asks (e.g., encrypted logging or restricted retention window), flag them now so I can include in the demo.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
